Definition: from G1722 and G4120; to entwine, i.e. (figuratively) involve with:--entangle (in, self with).
BiblicalUsage: To entwine, to get tangled up in. Paul says no soldier entangles himself with the affairs of this life in 2 Timothy 2:4, and Peter warns that those who escape the pollutions of the world and are again entangled in them end worse than they began in 2 Peter 2:20.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe entanglement is slow — nobody plans to be trapped, they just get busy with the affairs of this life until the snare closes, and I want to keep my hands free for the one who chose me to be His soldier.
